Heard Sri.Gopal Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the records.

2. This petition is filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C with the following prayer;
"WHEREFORE, the petitioner humbly pray before this Hon'ble Court to be pleased to allow the petition and be pleased to direct the respondent Commercial Street Police to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest in Crime No.12/2023 registered for offence punishable under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code submitted on the file of the XXIX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Mayohall at Bengaluru, imposing any conditions for which act of kindness the petitioner shall ever pray."

3. The brief facts of the case are as under; Sri.Neelesh Kothari lodged a complaint with Commercial Street Police Station on 08.02.2023, which was registered in Crime No.12/2023 for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC.
4.
Gist of the complaint averments reveal that the complainant is the native of Rajasthan State and about 35 years earlier, he came to Bengaluru and settled here for the business purpose.

On 01.02.2023, there was a call from the mobile No.7676568684 and wanted to purchase 14 gold chains and based on the same, on 02.02.2023 at about 3.45 p.m., the complainant was required to meet the said person near Commercial Street in front of Krishna Diamond Shop and the said person took 14 gold chains weighing about 468 grams and handed over the golden biscuit weighing 500 grams.
When the said gold biscuit was tested, later it appeared to be fake one.
Based on such complaint, the police registered the case against unknown persons at the first instance and apprehended Sri.Pavan Das.
Based on the voluntary statement given by Sri.Pavan Das, the present accused has been arrayed in the case and the police are trying to apprehend him.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner approached the District Court for grant of bail and same is rejected by order dated 13.03.2023 in Criminal Miscellaneous No.25197/2023.
Thereafter, the petitioner is before this Court.

sentences.text:
6. Reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, Sri.Gopal Singh learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently contended that the petitioner is totally innocent of the offences alleged against him and only on the basis of the voluntary statement given by accused No.1 - Pavan Das, he has been falsely implicated in the case and sought for grant of anticipatory bail.
7.
Per contra, the learned HCGP opposes the bail grounds.

8. Perused the materials on record meticulously in view of rival contentions of the parties.
9.
On such perusal of the materials on record, it is seen that initially, case came to be registered against unknown persons.
The police were able to apprehend one Pavandas.
Based on the voluntary statement, the present accused has been arrayed as accused No.2.
Whether at all, the offences alleged against the petitioner has committed or not, cannot be decided by this court at this stage by holding a mini trial.

It is for the Investigating Agency to investigate the matter and file appropriate report as contemplated under Section 172 of Cr.P.C.
10.
Suffice to say, the petitioner is not available to the investigating agency.
Therefore, directing the petitioner to join the investigation and to undergo limited period of custodial interrogation, would meet the ends of justice.

Accordingly, following order is passed;
ORDER
4. The petitioner shall co-operate with the Investigating Agency in all aspects of the matter including furnishing signature and thumb impression etc.,

Thereafter, the petitioner be enlarged on bail, by taking a bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum.
5. Petitioner shall attend the Court regularly.
6. Petitioner shall mark his attendance before the Investigating Officer on every alternate Sunday between 10.00 am and 2.00 pm., till the final report is filed.
7. Petitioner shall not directly or indirectly tamper the prosecution evidence or hamper the investigation process in any manner.
8. Petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of Bengaluru District without prior permission.
Violation of any one of the conditions would entitle the prosecution to seek for cancellation of the bail.
